The Goal:
The object of this contest is to make a tileset in 30 minutes. No more than 30 minutes, no less than 20 minutes, no exceptions. Then once you've made the tileset, you have 300 seocnds (5 minutes) to fill it in with objects, again no exceptions. It must be fun, and look good. It must be playable in userlevels as well. Old maps are allowed. Up to 3 submissions allowed. You must put a link to this contest in your submission(s). Judges may partake in this contest if they wish, although I personally wont!

The Deadline:
January 15, 2007
Judging begins January 20, 2007

The Scoring:
n/10 playability
n/10 as a tileset
n/10 originality


The Judges:
Me
29403
Empty
(If you wish to be a judge, just shoot me an email at kkstrong0@yahoo.com)

The Submissions:

Total: 0 Submissions

The Prizes:
1st place 3 deds.
2nd place sig 2 deds.
3rd place 1 ded.

Any questions? Did I forget to mention anything? If not, start map-making!

Some suggestions for bitesizers and All Numa Users in general

1) Maybe they should limit bitesizing priliges for the top 50 or 100 voters on NUMA, or set a limit, that once your have 1000, 2000, or even 3000 votes, you can get a special account. This is to ensure that bitesize accounts will know NUMA fairly well, and will have devoted enough time to it. The only problem with that is that much sniping would happen just to get to that limit to have the special account.

2) Adding on to my last idea, maybe the only people who can get bitesize account at people with over 1500 votes, an average rating of at least 3.5, at least 3-5 maps bitesized, and have over 25 rated maps. And then adding ont to that, then onlythe people who ask and are approved

3) I personally like the integration of bitesize, becuase its no longer a hassle to bitesize, and look at the bitesized maps either

4) Maybe there should be a need for multiple bitesizers to bitesize a map, but no more than three for one map, this ensures that a bitesized map truly deserves it. This only problem with that is that there is might be some people with that many bitesizer friends who are willing

5) Maybe they should make it so that you can only bitesize one every ten or twenty maps made. The only problem with that is that if somebody is really wanting to bitesize something, and has already bitesized previously recently before, then they can't, no matter how good the map is!

6) Maybe there should be a limit to how many maps you can bitesize in a week. Such as, you have reached your limit of 3 bitesized maps this week, sorry you may not bitesize this map. Read Numero 5 for the problem with that suggestion though!

I'd like to hear some feedback on these suggestions!!!

#311310 6 2007-04-08T16:53:18Z kkstrong0
To Watch Demos

1. Open the game
2. Press "\"
3. In the top box, enter the desired map data
4. Press "L"
5. In the bottom box, enter the demo replay data
6. Press "3"
7. Press "Q"
8. Press "P"
9. Make Sure Caps is ON

To Make Demos

1. Open the game
2. Press "\"
3. In the top box, enter the desired map data
4. Press "L"
5. Press "R"
6. Press "W"
7. Press "1"
8. Press "P"
9. Make Sure Caps is ON
10. Repeat until you have the desired demo
11. Submit to NUMA with a comment and a rating (hehe!)

to create a map, first have an idea, then go into N, press "\", then press insert or delete depending on if you want to make tiles or objects and press number dependingf on which tile or object you want to make, and make your map, then playtest, then submit the data that you get from the upper righthand box (i.e. copy and paste) in to the submit a map section in NUMA, then fill in a title and description,a nd press submit, and thats all

the process can take anywhere between 5 minutes and 100 hours

Moving Walls

One very special usage of thwumps which many great DDA makers love to use is called the Moving Wall method. It�s becoming more common, and was popularized by Lucidium�s Pressed for Time. When placed in a specific area, half-way engulfed in a tile, a thwump is placed facing the inside of the wall. See this diagram.



In the diagram above, as long as there is any tile in the red area, the thwump will move in the direction of the arrow when touched. In the last two cases, a little more care is needed when placing the thwumps. They will not obey the special �Moving Wall� rules if they are placed using 1/2 snap. The third thwump in the diagram must be placed exactly one pixel above its 1/2 snap position to work. The last thwump must be placed exactly one pixel left of its 1/2 snap position to work. Both of these can be done by code-editing. Knowing that the 2 numbers directly after the 8^ represent the x- and y-coordinates of the object, you know how to manipulate its position to move it one pixel in the direction you want (you�ll be subtracting 1 to do this either way, from the x-coordinate for a leftward moving wall, or from the y-coordinate for an upward moving wall). This is a map with plenty of moving walls to demonstrate their impact in a DDA.

Quote: Kablizzy, June 04, 2007 08:35 am
Simplicity - Minimalism makes packs. Long maps don't belong in map packs. Packs, more often than not, are meant to be played as a whole, rather than just a conglomeration of maps. If it were just a smattering of different maps, you'd be better suited to submit them to NUMA as a series.
I completely disagree with this point.

I think map packs with mainly simple maps are the packs that suffer the worst. Long maps can often be the maps that make a map pack memorable. Simple maps just fly by in a flurry, and don't leave a lasting impression. It's the maps that people spend time on, or introduce a new concept that really hold people. I think maps that are just 'simple' are usually fillers made to take up space so that a mapper can reach his target number of levels. A pack of simple maps can work, but that is to say, they usually work as a group of simple maps. I think it's the long maps that really make a pack what it is.

My Top 10 Door Related Requests for N+ and N 1.5

1. Switches which can be toggled on and off, so a door can be repeatedly opened and closed

2. Having more than one switch operate a single door

3. Better NED allowing movement of doors by dragging and dropping doors, as opposed to deleting a door using its switch, and remaking it, which can be a nightmare if there are many switches in a single tile area

4. For the trap door switch: When pressed the switch becomes grey, just like the locked door switch

5. Doors which span more than one tile, imagine 5 tile long doors, they could really help with the feeling of scale in some levels

6. Timed doors, which open only after a pre-defined delay

7. Doors which are opened only after many switches have been pressed

8. Diagonally placable doors

9. Doors which require all the gold in a room to be collected before they open

10. Differently coloured trigger lines in NED for every single door

        #349590 95 2007-08-01T02:21:26Z kkstrong0
        Feedback?

        Ok i can give feedback

        I like some of the maps more than the other, but something that really bothered me was that I was not able to figure out how to do the one about the piece in a puzzle, its was rather frustrating and aggravating for me to try because no matter how hard I jump, I could get neither the switch nor the column of gold over the switch, so a demo would be much appreciated

        I liked alone in the City, it was a good difficultly level and it was rather hard, the gold was a good idea, however, I think it would have been better without the drone that started on the top that revolved around the e tile, but overall it was a good level

        Aspen was also a good level, i felt that the gauss behind the thwump was unneeded, and i didnt like that part, the gold and mine placement was ingenious, and the "1" tile set made a good tile set, the thumps were poorly placed, and only one would have been needed

        On the other hand, BOO was a awful level, there were no aspects of this level that I enjoyed, everything seemed to randomly placed and the tile set was horrendous, it was just an overall "no-no" the one thing that i like about this level was the beginning, I liked how you get one jump to gather your thoughts before the rocket comes after you

        Circular was one of my favorite levels, i played this for about 10 minutes trying to improve my score, the only this in that the rocket felt useless because with just a normal route of the holding right at the start the rocket just goes through the one ways and curves away from the ninja, never to be seen again

        On Description of a Car Struggles, hehe, I love the name! it was overall was difficult level, I found that the easiest way to get over the mine and one ways at the top is to was to go the level with the rightmost switch and jump off that corner, this was one of your best levels in the set of 25

        I liked the level drowning, it provided the good challenge, but the gauss should have been placed elsewhere, maybe on the right most diagonal in between the 2 different types of switches

        Floor pie was an interesting level also, my only thing i would have tweaked if I had made the level is that I would have made the gauss a rocket, this makes it much harder yes, but rocket dodging is one of my favorite things to do

        Joseph was a good level, but it almost looks like it was lv generator tile set, just cleaned up, but I dont see any problems with that. The rocket/normal door combination was genius, and so were the squares on the bottom of gold the rocket dodging a the bottom pocket was the most fun part of the level, but I didnt quite understand the area on the right, it looked randomly placed and the trapdoor were unneeded, so psh!, but a fun level nevertheless

        Lamb Chop in a Slasher Flick was a fun level, the three rockets and the huge amounts of gold were interesting. My only qualm with this level is the gauss, that should not have been their at all, the level that single gauss make the level extremely hard even without the gold or the three rockets and the right of the map with the gold

        Le Den was a fun level, but i think the chain gun should have been rocket, and the tile set should have been neater, i just plain didn't like the tiles, they werent fun or good for the map type, the chain gun is hard enough to get past without having to deal with choppy tiles

        Light on your limbs was a GREAT level, i really enjoyed the tile set, and the four drones made the map challenging, but also fun. The bad thing about this level, it that they all followed the same path, making them far to predictable

        I really enjoyed Little Rwanda, but i feel that there were not enough leasers in the level, it was far to easy just to slip by them when going for the gold, maybe eight would have been a better number? oh well, still a AWESOME level, it also looks like it could have been something that i would have made

        Music in a Box was another one of my favorite levels; I cant tell you enough how much i enjoy cramped levels with moving drones in them, FUN FUN FUN FUN FUN FUN FUN, and did I mention this level was fun! I also really like curves, it look s like these some of these maps are delving into my style to end up like something Id make

        OMGFGFIFTY was a funny level, i did not like the multitude of launch pad though, maybe one or two edited launch pads would have been better, the only was i found to complete the level was to corner kick after jumping back onto the bottom launch pad, ingenious, although this was not difficult for me, it might have been too difficult for some other people, so Id watch it when going into corner kicks and corner jumping

        ONETWOTHREEFOURFIVESIXSEVENGNGBANG was not a fun level, I ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS hate chain guns layered upon each other, no good no good no good, make maybe two chain guns (which is plenty) and put the going in different direction, so the entire map is difficult, not just the one part

        Peninsula was and okay map, though not your best I think some one ways or trapdoor would have worked better to get the ninja to the gold, and some mines on the bottom would have been nice

        Rollin' Rollin' Rollin' was a good map, but i did not enjoy the concept multiple bounce block made the map too hard, and it was just plain not good, maybe taking out most of the bounce block and making the gauss a rocket would have fit better with the maps

        Searching for Disrobe was a great map, with a great concept, but maybe layering the bounce on the outside so as to keep the ninja in would have been better, but when I completed it the first time i cheated by going outside the arena and waiting fro the drones to pass, then getting the switch and getting to the door before the drones came back, it was far tooooooo easy to cheat

        Sis was a good level, though more effort should have been put into it, I found that it was easy to beat by just hitting the left button and the right buttons when appropriate, it was just too easy, i dont know how you could have make it harder though, soorry

        Sprite Club was another one of those maps of your that i really enjoyed the drones moving together make the whole map look like a well oiled machine or that the drones are somehow moving from block to block, it just created a great illusion, but the maps was too easy again. Also the gold was too difficult to get, but maybe thats just me? The lag for some computer might be unbearable but it only gets my lag to 13 ms/f YAY laptop

        Stand down was a great level, but over it felt like it was a luck level, you just sorta have to pray that the laser points toward the wall on this second shot at you, hmm, I dont this there is any way that I would change this, yummy sexalicious level

        The unoriginal 2x2 level was original, I enjoy trying to find new ways to get past the rocket, get the switch and get to the door in only one jump, but alas i failed, great level, boy I am getting tired of typing this all or you, I sure hope you enjoy it and learn for the comment I am giving here and now

        three was a fun level, but again too many drones, that seem to be a common theme among your drone maps, hmm ....the top thwump with the switch over it was unneeded and should have been put in the same direction as the rest of the thwump lower in the level, but it was a huge hindrance. Also you should not have made getting up so easy, it was just too easy of a map i felt

        Tripo was a good, level although it was difficult i enjoying the concept, but it was poor execution the rocket placement was messy, and I would have done them in some formation or something like that. I dont know what else to say about it other than the gold placement was good, not great just good, i like clumps of gold like that, it makes me feel reassured that i will be able to finish the map with enough time left

        Is that enough feedback for you, huh?

        #17200 1 2007-09-13T05:57:59Z kkstrong0
        This morning I think I broke my mothers nose on accident, we were in an argument and I was trying to push her face out of my face, and was going for her forehead, but I guess i hit her eyes/upper nose, and she thinks i broke it, and well, I dont really know. But anyways back on topic, up until yesterday I had no idea why she was this way or who she was before I was born, so then the perfect assignment for class (Bible) was assigned. the assignment was to write a story describing a member of you family, and was only supposed to be 1 paragraph long, but me being the geeek I am, ended up writing 7 pages (double spaced) and I was pretty proud of it, so here it is. I am considering using it for my common apps (for college), but of course in much greater detail. This is an extremely condesned version of the story.

        Well anyways, I would like to take this post to hear about other people's family's, no names are needed, just a brief (or not so brief!) story would be great, I would love to read them all, and I will enjoy it too! I now have a great new respect for my mother, after knowing the hardships she went through before having me, and it has brought us closer together. I only wish to share this joy that I have found with my mother, so either go down and ask your mother about her life before you, or for you all to take a moment and examine how great you mother really is!

        So without further ado, here is the story:

        When I first set out on this journey to find a story, I honestly had no idea what I was going to talk about. I was truly perplexed, what it that made my family its quirky self? I called my grandmother who lives in San Diego and visits our house for the weekend every weekend. My grandmother told me her story wasnt nearly interesting enough for this homework assignment. After much badgering for her to give me any great ideas she said to go talk to my mother about her life before I was born. Honestly, I was not terribly intrigued by the idea, after over the years, not hearing very many great things, only that my mothers pre-me life was extremely exciting, but I did not know much more than that, nor had I ever questioned her about it, so I figured now would be a great time to ask her all about her life. What she told me was an hour long story and I shall try to abridge the version of the story she gave me because I have to admit, it was a fairly interesting life she had before me. So I will begin now telling you the story of her high school days all the way to my conceiving:

        Her story began when she was in her senior year of high school. She graduated from a small high school in San Diego, about 10 miles away from SDSU called Patrick Henry high school. Her father (my grandpa) was fairly sexist so he told her that if she went to college she wouldnt be financially supported by him, and she would be cut off nearly completely, but that didnt matter to her because she had received a large scholarship from scoring well on the PSAT/NMSQT while in high school. This scholarship funded her completely through four years of college in any University of California School. She choose the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), mainly because her father (my grandpa) did not want her to become a Nuclear Engineer, as he had been all of his life. UCSB had a great program for exactly this major, and because she wanted rebellion so badly she took this up as something she wanted to learn. So she applied for UCSB and was accepted (being a straight A student in high school) and began to major in Nuclear Engineering. At the time it was very rare for any woman to take on this major, as well as it was a fairly rare major overall, only being offered by 3 universities in the country.

        In her sophomore year, she decided to study a year abroad as her scholarship covered a year abroad, so she decided it would be fun, and she should take advantage of the opportunity that lay in front of her. As she went on to through college she decided with a few of her friends to start up a branch of the pre-existing club Society of Women Engineers (SWE) which promotes both womens right and more specifically Women Engineers. This club is still going on today, after being started in 1977 with my mother as the first president of the Santa Barbra branch. This was in her junior year (3rd) out of 5 years she spent in college. She spent a year more in college because she decided to take a year abroad and although the stuff she was learning in Sweden was great and all, it did not fit in the strict schedule of items you have to learn in succession to become a Nuclear Engineer. The year abroad cost her an extra year that she had to pay through herself because her scholarship no longer supported her.

        To gain some access to some money, she decided it would be a great opportunity to join the ROTC program at her school and commit herself to 4 more years of $600/month pay which was double what she was living off of at the time in the ROTC program, but there was a problem. My mother wished to be proactive at this time and the Nuclear Navy program she considered joining wanted to ground her because all the Nuclear programs was on the front line (which she had no problem with). At the time only men went on the front-line so she would be grounded to teaching for 4 years in Florida, and this did not even sound fun to her, so she decided not to take the position, because as you can see by her starting the SWE program she was fairly proactive about womens rights.

        She decided she would be better suited somewhere else. The previous president at the time was Carter who signed a law that started affirmative action, which was a law that forced companies to have a certain amount of women to men ratio in a business to get a grant from the government which helped to a great degree. Now this was difficult from the nuclear businesses to comply with because here were so few women who were Nuclear Engineering majors in the entire country. The shortage of women was to such a degree that not everyone could get enough women to sign onto the affirmative action, so all women Nuclear engineering were in extremely high demand. My mother was starting her fifth year of college at this point and every Friday another business would fly her all around the country for the weekend on their tab to go for an interview, so she went to New York, Texas, Utah, Florida, etc. around the entire country for all these interviews because she was in such high demand for all the companies. She knew that she was only getting all these interviews and all these weekends stays around the country because she was a woman, and she didnt like this much and she decided not to take any of these offers up.

        What she later found out about affirmative action would change her life: this law did not apply to any company who had less than 50 employees. So she found a company of this sort who obviously wanted her because she was well qualified, and not specifically because she was a woman. She found this to her liking, and on top of this personal bonus she gained, the company offered to match any salary of the top offer, knowing she was in high demand. She took a liking to this company because they didnt want her because she was a woman, but because she was a great engineer ranked 3rd in her class so this was a huge plus for her. So after she was done with her schooling, she took a job as a Nuclear Engineer, which slowly turned into a Uranium and Plutonium Broker. This job description included selling the pure uranium and plutonium ores that were mined around the country in hundreds of tiny mines. She worked at this job until a huge slab of pure uranium was found in Canada (which is still supplying Uranium to the world over 25 years later). The hundreds of tiny mines could not hope to compete with this huge mine, so she as a broker was run out of the business. On a stroke on good luck I guess it was, four cities in Texas ended up buying about 2 million pounds of uranium before they were ready to use it, thinking their power plant (which needs the uranium to run) would be completed soon. As it turned out the power plants would not be finished for another 10 years after that (late 1980s), so they needed a broker to come down and sell this overload of uranium. What happened was that their was no longer any buyer because of this Canadian mine, so she eventually gave up trying to sell it, so she again was offered a job to help with the actual building of the power plants. She did this for quite some time before she because bored with the business.

        She then enrolled into law school, where she worked at the power plant by day, and studied law by night. When I asked her when she slept, she told me, Whenever I could! So after she graduated from law school, she moved back to California, where she learned to practice Californian law (which is different than Texas law), and she began at a law firm called OMelveny and Meyers. This particular law firm is in Los Angeles, California and is famous for representing large companies who are having legal troubles all around the country. Mostly it dispatches lawyers to around the country on extremely short notice, where they have to familiarize themselves with the lawsuit and work night and day until they come up with a defense for the large companies.

        So finally one day, she was dispatched to work in Albuquerque, New Mexico. This was a fateful case that started just regularly, but would change her life forever yet again. The case was in the middle of trial and she was expected to stay in New Mexico for another 3 months, when suddenly the case settled in the middle of the trial, surprisingly and unexpectedly. Her bosses gave her and her co-workers the next amount of time off (up until the trial would have ended) as they had nothing else for those lawyers to do. Another reason why they did this is because the law office was in the middle of switching management because her boss had been elected as secretary of state and took many layers with him to become his cabinet.

        My mother decided to become a little more spontaneous with her life and took the next plane to as far away as she could get. The next day she was on a plane to Nepal for a two week vacation of hiking through the Himalaya Mountains. Nepal is a small Asian country just north of India and west of China. There she met the man she thought she would spend the rest of her life with, her tour guide (called a Sherpa in Nepal). His name was Deepak Chettri (Dee-Pah-K Chet-Tree) and she acquired a visa for him (having connections with the Secretary of Defense and his workers) in about a week. This process usually works in only about a year, but it sure does help to have friends in high places! So they moved back to America, and exactly on their 80th day together back in the United States they became married. I was born very shortly after they were married and my father stayed around town for the first 3 months of my life, before me mother caught him stealing from her, and Deepak went back to Nepal. This was mainly because he conveniently began to start feel homesick after him and my mother divorced each other. Then my mother was still working at her prestigious law-firm OMelveny and Meyers.

        When I was approaching one years old, they asked my mother to move to Alaska with me so that she could represent people who committed the Exxon Valdez Oil Spill, and my mother decided Alaska was not the best place for me to grow up, and she quit her law-firm knowing her working such long hours and moving at a moments notice was not the best environment to grow up in for a 1 year old. She quit her job at her law-firm and moved to San Diego, where she grew up for most of her life. She joined a law-firm who hired her in San Diego, and thats where I spent the first 6 or so years of my life. So thats the end of this story, and thats a family story if I have ever heard one!

        #457929 5 2008-08-03T20:22:52Z kkstrong0
        Everything you need is on the Map description

        Text Drone : 6^x,y,Path,1,201,direction^textArray,x_offset,y_offset,align,border,textColor,backgroundColor,fontSize,font,bold,italic,underline 

Apart from textArray, all other paramters are optional 

textArray: escaped text characters joined by ":" 
align: 0=left, 1=center, 2=right 
border: 0= no border, 1=has border 
textColor & backgroundColor: from 000000 to FFFFFF 
font: _sans, _serif, _typewriter , if you put other fonts, other players may not able to see it 
bold,italic,underline : 0 or 1 

specialOn Trigger: Display next text in array 
SpecialOff Trigger: Hiding the text 

escape your text: 
http://n.infunity.com/swf/escape.swf

        I hereby apply for a staff position.

        I have had a chance to dabble in NUMA staffing, so I have some knowledge on what goes on behind the scenes, and I also gained quite a bit of experience. I would say the best thing I learned from being a part of the NUMA staff was learning from my mistakes. As you all know, I made one big mistake, and it cost me the position. Thats the best thing I learned from the position. I learned exactly what you can and cannot do, that is super important. I have made my mistakes, and I now have learned from them. Thats not something you can get from someone who has just been on the forums, or even who has staffing experience. You have to make mistakes to learn, unfortunately for me, it was a big mistake. I know you will consider this when considering my application, but please don't make that the deal breaker, even though I do realize it is a huge stain on my track record.

        For the past year and a half or so, I have been and still remain to be one of the more active members of this forum. I spend a great deal of my time, here, and I wish to make this forum a better place for all. These forums really need someone who knows these forums inside and out, and I feel that I do.

        Another reason why I feel I am ready for this position is because I love Metanet. I want to do everything I can to make it a better place for all people, and I have a few ideas, being from the lower castes of Metanet, that I could bring forward as a Metanet forums staff member.

        Yet another reason why I am a great person to consider for this application is because more than anything, I really want it. It is my belief that you can't succeed, unless you really want to achieve your goal. The same applies here. It has been a dream of mine to be a staffer here and now is my chance. Most say its not as glamorous as it sounds, but what another thing I learned from my previous experience was this: It becomes glamorous if you love what you are doing, and really it doesn't matter, you just have to love it. I know I love this place, I know I do.

        Thank-you for considering this application.
        - Kkstrong0
